subject: About interpretation of K and loadings in PACA

messages.author: 333f3e76f253995a
messages.subject: About interpretation of K and loadings in PACA
parts:
Hello everybody, I am running a PACA on log-shape ratios of linear skull measurements. The data has a strong phylogenetic signal (Kmult: 1.6266, P-value: 0.001) with a considerable effect size 5.1437. Moreover, the K on the first component is quite large 2.603, and then drops down to 0.48 in K2. So, I assume that the signal was concentrated in some variables of the original data (similar to empiric example 1 in Collyer and Admas 2020). In the context of PACA, is valid to analyze the loadings in the first component in search of the variable who most contribute to component 1, or in this case, in the phylogenetic signal?

Kind regards,

Ale

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] About interpretation of K and loadings in PACA
parts:
Dear Ale,

YES!

That would be a fantastic inferential path to follow.  You might find though that several correlated variables are what concentrate that signal, not just one.

This is the kind of analysis we hoped PACA would inspire.

Cheers!
Mike
